correctness.rationale: For adjacent k-token states sharing core I, any common neighbor outside that core would contain both endpoints of a sliding edge and violate independence. Thus every clique of size >=2 has a unique (k-1)-core. An induced diamond in TS then forces one in G. Maximal cliques of diamond-free graphs meet only at vertices, so each simplex collapses to a tree of edges. Counting unused rook rows/columns yields the all-clique polynomial; connectivity and star-transposition boundaries give graph topology, girth, diameter and four-cycle count. Rook corner cases k=1 and m=n=k follow from direct move enumeration; finite checker is only corroboration.
